title: Conormal sheaf of the diagonal and relative differentials
statement: Let f:X\to S be a morphism of schemes [def-pc-scheme], and let \Delta:X\to X\times_S X be its diagonal [def-pc-base-change]. The conormal sheaf C_\Delta of this immersion is defined locally by choosing an open neighbourhood W of \Delta(X) in X\times_S X on which \Delta is a closed immersion, with ideal sheaf \mathcal I, and setting C_\Delta=\Delta^*(\mathcal I/\mathcal I^2) [def-pc-module-pullback]; this is independent of the choice of W. Define the relative Kähler differential sheaf \Omega^1_{X/S} by requiring that on every affine U=\operatorname{Spec}(A)\subseteq X mapping into an affine V=\operatorname{Spec}(R)\subseteq S, it is the sheaf associated to the A-module of Kähler differentials \Omega_{A/R} [def-weil-pbc-kahler-differentials]. Then there is a canonical isomorphism C_\Delta\cong\Omega^1_{X/S}.

source.place: Tag 08S2 (conormal sheaf of the diagonal is the sheaf of relative differentials)

proof.text: Choose a normalized difference derivation from lem-sc-diagonal-conormal-derivation-exists. Apply the existing universal property relativeDifferentialsHomEquiv to obtain a morphism from relative differentials to the diagonal conormal.
For every affine U mapping into an affine V, lem-sc-diagonal-conormal-affine-comparison gives bijectivity of the comparison on sections.

The adapted affine opens form a basis: for a point in an arbitrary open, choose an affine neighbourhood V of its image and an affine neighbourhood U of the point contained in the intersection with f⁻¹V. Apply Mathlib TopCat.Sheaf.isIso_iff_isIso_basis to the underlying abelian sheaf map, reflect the isomorphism back to module sheaves using Modules.toPresheaf, and invert it for the asserted orientation.
